user_signal.goal_or_constraint: Once a plausible system defect enters maintenance, execution must follow a durable non-skippable SOP instead of depending on memory, recall, checklist discipline, or post-hoc record completion.
user_signal.counterexample: Universal already had triage, parent-system reframing, learning and meta-maintenance checks, yet a model could still enter maintenance, act out of order, and only later produce a structurally complete report. This means detection/recall and execution control were conflated.
user_signal.proposed_mechanism: Keep ingress triage thin, then route confirmed systemic maintenance through one deterministic durable controller whose canonical stages come from SYSTEM_MAINTENANCE_POLICY, with prepatch checkpointing, reopen semantics and closure binding.

system_impact_map: durable controller state and cross-chat recovery
validation failure reopen and downstream receipt invalidation
shared-method propagation to current BUSINESS owners without business-state mutation
falsification_checks: NO_DEFECT must not enter systemic maintenance or authorize patching.
INVESTIGATE must be evidence-only and must not pre-complete canonical systemic stages.
CONFIRMED_DEFECT must not skip or reorder canonical stages.
M7 implementation must not be authorized until a durable prepatch checkpoint exists and has been authoritatively reread.
Validation failure must reopen the repair loop and invalidate downstream receipts instead of continuing to closure.
A second-order newly discovered systemic gap must be able to reopen an earlier stage and require revalidation.
The current persisted controller state itself must be directly validated by CI, not only controller fixtures.
A closed current meta run must be bound to a complete controller trace once the controller contract is activated.
A duplicate maintenance SOP/controller must be removed rather than retained as a shadow authority.
Repository enforcement must not be overstated as GitHub server-side branch protection or platform tool-call interception.

failure_history.escalation_reason: V61 already reached META_METHOD by requiring historical failure-class recall and abstraction escalation. The new counterexample shows that even correct diagnosis methodology can be bypassed if execution remains a policy/checklist plus post-hoc verifier. There is no higher named abstraction level, so the meta-method itself was redesigned around a runtime stage controller.
failure_history.class_level_prevention: Separate three responsibilities: thin ingress triage decides whether maintenance is relevant; the durable maintenance controller governs ordered in-run execution and patch authorization; meta-governance/CI validate closure and assurance. History/recall is diagnostic input only and cannot substitute for execution control.
failure_history.instance_fix: The canonical runtime/maintenance_controller.py was hardened for a strict INVESTIGATE state, verified durable prepatch admission, reopen-safe revision semantics and explicit action authorization. A duplicate maintenance_sop implementation created during this repair was physically deleted. The current controller state was made durable, declared in AGENT_MANIFEST, directly validated by CI, self-hosted through M0-M11, and reopened from second-order review when a persisted-state validation gap was discovered.

sources.observation: Historical recall and abstraction escalation improve diagnosis but do not themselves make execution non-skippable.
sources.rationale: Retain historical matching as a diagnostic input while moving execution ordering to the controller.

sources.observation: Durable workflow event history supports reconstruction of workflow state after interruption rather than relying on transient process memory.
sources.rationale: Adopt the durable-state principle only; Universal does not adopt Temporal as an authority or dependency.

sources.observation: Explicit workflow errors and recovery transitions make failure handling part of the state machine instead of letting execution implicitly continue.
sources.rationale: Adopt explicit reopen/fail-closed transition semantics only; Universal does not import the Step Functions framework.

rejected_existing_candidates: Recall/reminder expansion was rejected because it cannot guarantee post-entry execution order.
A new supervisor/reflection Agent was rejected because it adds another actor without deterministic transition enforcement.
A second maintenance_sop runtime was rejected and deleted because it duplicated the existing canonical controller.
capability_reuse.rationale: The repository already contained the correct owner surface: one maintenance controller plus one post-hoc meta verifier. Extending these existing mechanisms is smaller and more enforceable than adding another Agent, policy, registry or parallel SOP.

verified_facts: ENTRYPOINT and STARTUP_HOOK already separate cheap defect triage from full maintenance activation.
Before this repair the canonical controller did not fully model INVESTIGATE as evidence-only and did not require a durable prepatch checkpoint.
The repair physically removed a duplicate maintenance_sop mechanism instead of keeping two SOP authorities.
The self-hosted controller run persisted M0-M6A before implementation, bound a verified prepatch checkpoint to commit 7155f4aacc0238a7fe308f58959cfc4d60498007, then executed M7 onward.
Second-order review reopened the run to M7 after detecting that current durable controller state was not directly under CI; the second validation run then passed with 295 tests.
GitHub main is currently unprotected, so repository logic cannot be represented as server-side branch protection.
No BUSINESS lease or business truth was changed by this maintenance run.
unresolved_facts: The repository cannot independently prove that the latest STARTUP_HOOK text is installed in account-level Custom Instructions.

The current GitHub connector does not expose a configurable pre-action middleware hook that can physically block every direct model-initiated GitHub mutation before the repository controller is consulted.
Independent semantic correctness of diagnosis is not established by the same-repository controller and CI.
A future ordinary user message still needs live product evidence that thin ingress triage enters the controller automatically without the user explicitly saying this is a system defect.
autonomous_next_steps: Activate the controller contract in the authoritative task manifest only after the final controller state and V62 meta run are durable.
Run closure CI with the controller-complete binding gate enabled.
Keep platform/account and GitHub server-side enforcement boundaries explicit rather than compensating with another repository Agent.

alternatives.rationale: Useful for diagnosis but still lets an entered maintenance run skip, reorder or reconstruct steps after the fact.
Adds coordination and duplicate authority; a duplicate SOP created during the repair was deleted after reuse scan found the existing controller.

Makes responsibilities explicit and testable with fewer active mechanisms: ingress decides whether to enter, controller governs execution, durable state supports resume/reopen, and meta/CI prevent false closure.

architecture_payoff.current_failure_cost: Users repeatedly identify that a known system problem was entered but not fully executed; post-hoc reports can look complete even when pre-action sequencing was not enforced.
architecture_payoff.change_cost: Harden one existing controller, add one task-local durable controller-state surface, extend existing tests/manifest wiring, and delete the accidental duplicate SOP.
architecture_payoff.expected_payoff: Systemic maintenance gains explicit stateful execution semantics without putting the full governance loop on normal business turns and without adding another permanent Agent or root policy.
architecture_payoff.deletion_or_simplification_result: runtime/maintenance_sop.py and tests/test_maintenance_sop.py were deleted. The surviving architecture is one policy owner, one during-execution controller, one durable task-local state, and the existing post-hoc meta/CI verifier.

instruction_surface.reason: The current repository STARTUP_HOOK already contains the thin per-material-input defect preflight and delegates detailed maintenance to repository authority. Additional prompt growth would duplicate the controller. Product installation/readback of that hook remains a separate external evidence boundary.

propagation.mechanism: The shared invariant propagates through Universal operational_hygiene/evolution contracts and routing. The controller remains Universal-owned; owner-local business workflows, leases, facts and evidence are not copied or mutated.

superseded_or_demoted_surfaces: runtime/maintenance_sop.py deleted as duplicate controller authority.
tests/test_maintenance_sop.py deleted with the duplicate implementation.
Post-hoc meta record completeness alone is no longer treated as sufficient evidence of ordered in-run execution once the controller contract is activated.
Recall/history is demoted from an implied execution guarantee to a diagnosis input.

second_order_findings: The first pass validated controller code but not the live persisted controller state; M10 therefore reopened M7, added a current-state conformance test, invalidated downstream receipts and reran validation to 295 passing tests.
An accidental second SOP implementation was itself evidence of governance-bloat risk; it was deleted rather than maintained as a compatibility layer.
INVESTIGATE must be modeled as a separate evidence state; allowing it to prefill systemic stages would make the controller look strict while preserving post-hoc behavior.
A durable prepatch checkpoint is needed because in-memory stage order does not prove that the system could recover the same admission state after chat interruption.

Repository-level controller enforcement is not equivalent to GitHub server-side branch protection or platform-level tool-call interception; main is currently unprotected and that boundary remains open.
Independent semantic diagnosis quality remains outside the assurance provided by deterministic controller/CI conformance.

maintenance_controller.self_host_boundary: The early bootstrap repair before durable controller state creation is not retroactively claimed as controller-governed. The self-hosted controller trace begins with the durable M0-M6A state written before subsequent implementation and continues through a real M10->M7 reopen and second validation cycle.

Kept the account hook to cheap triage; detailed SOP remains repository-owned.

Deleted the duplicate SOP and retained only the canonical controller.

Hardened the single canonical controller, removed duplicate SOP authority, bound durable controller state into Universal architecture, required complete controller trace before future closed meta-run binding, and added CI validation of the current persisted controller state itself.

Second-cycle hosted validation passed risk-tiered control-plane audit, Agent architecture harness, and full pytest with 295 passed, including direct validation of the current persisted controller state.

Reverified shared-method propagation after the M7 reopen. The controller remains Universal-owned and all current BUSINESS owners inherit the shared maintenance/evolution invariant through Universal contracts/routing; no BUSINESS lease or business-truth mutation was performed.

Second-order review reopened M7 once to close the persisted-state validation gap, then revalidated the system. No duplicate SOP, shadow stage authority, owner-local controller copy, startup bloat, or BUSINESS mutation remains in scope. Assurance is regression-verified execution control, not independent semantic proof or unbypassable tool-level enforcement; direct external GitHub mutations remain a declared open boundary while main is unprotected.

Persisted the execution lesson as runtime state-machine behavior: recall/history helps diagnose; the controller enforces ordered execution; durable checkpointing preserves position; reopen invalidates stale downstream evidence; meta/CI gate closure. Remaining product and GitHub enforcement boundaries stay explicit rather than being hidden by more governance layers.

closure.unknown_or_open_world_boundary: The controller closes the repository-level SOP execution gap for compliant Universal maintenance and makes ordered execution/reopen/closure evidence testable. It does not make the model or GitHub platform globally incapable of bypassing repository code, guarantee perfect defect classification, or prove future product-level activation until observed.
